Job Title: HR Operations SpecialistÂ 

Type: Independent ContractorÂ 

Location: Remote | South Africa

About Us

The Law Offices of Sabrina Li, P.C. is a leading, full-service U.S. immigration law firm with offices in Los Angeles, Pasadena, Santa Ana, and Dallas, as well as international operations across Asia, Africa, and Central and South America. We are dedicated to helping individuals, families, and businesses navigate complex legal challenges with skill, compassion, and integrity.

We are proud to be recognized as a 2025 Inc. Best Workplaces honoree, a distinction that reflects our intentional investment in our people and workplace culture. Our firm prioritizes professional development, clear career pathways, and a culture of accountability and respectâcreating a workplace where high performers can build meaningful, long-term careers.

The Opportunity

We are seeking a tech-savvy, proactive HR professional with excellent communication skills to support our HR team across recruitment, onboarding, compliance, and training. You'll work alongside firm leadership to keep day-to-day HR operations running smoothly and help identify smarter, more efficient ways to manage HR processes using AI and automation.

If you enjoy variety in your work, thrive on process and organization, adapt quickly to new tools, and want to grow with a firm that invests in its people, this role is a great fit.

Key Responsibilities

HR Operations & Compliance

  • Support the employee onboarding process, helping new hires get set up and proficient with the firm's technology stack within their first week.
  • Assist with HR document, process, and compliance audits, and monitor completion of required documentation, certifications, training, and policy acknowledgements.
  • Follow up with employees and managers on outstanding compliance items.
  • Maintain accurate HR records within Rippling and other HR systems.

Recruitment & Talent Support

  • Support sourcing for open roles, including candidate outreach and headhunting for hard-to-fill positions when standard applicant pipelines fall short.
  • Help manage candidate pipelines and keep hiring managers updated on status.
  • Assist with background and reference checks and credential verification.
  • Participate in candidate interviews alongside hiring managers.

Training & Development

  • Help maintain and update the firm's training curriculum, onboarding materials, and learning resources.
  • Assist in creating SOPs, workflow documentation, process maps, and training materials as needed.
  • Support the development of assessments and knowledge checks to track training completion.

Process Improvement & Automation

  • Identify opportunities to streamline HR workflows through automation and AI-powered tools.
  • Help maintain workflows within monday.com and other operational platforms.

Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in Psychology, Human Resources, Business Administration, Management, or a related field (required).
  • Tech-savvy, with the ability to quickly learn and adapt to new tools, systems, and platforms (required).
  • Excellent written and spoken English with strong, proactive communication skills â comfortable flagging issues, asking questions, and following up without being prompted (required).
  • Proactive and self-directed, able to anticipate needs and take initiative in a fast-paced, fully remote environment (required).
  • Minimum of 2 years of experience in HR operations for a U.S.-based company, including onboarding, compliance, or employee lifecycle support (required).
  • Experience using monday.com and HRIS platforms such as Rippling (required).
  • Experience creating clear documentation, SOPs, or process materials.
  • Comfortable using AI tools to support content creation, documentation, and process efficiency.
  • Strong attention to detail and ability to manage multiple priorities.
  • Preferred: recruitment or sourcing experience, including candidate outreach, vetting, and interviewing.
  • Preferred: experience with Canva or similar tools for training or communication materials.

Why Join Our Team?

  • Stable, remote opportunity to work with a well-established U.S.-based law firm that values continuous learning, innovation, and professional growth.
  • Competitive compensation with performance-based bonuses.
  • Fully remote role within a diverse global team.
  • Paid time off, including U.S. federal holidays, sick leave, and annual leave.
  • Pacific Time-aligned working hours with reasonable flexibility.
  • Opportunity to grow with the firm's HR function as it scales.
  • Structured onboarding and clear expectations from day one.
  • Stable, long-term opportunity with a growing U.S. law firm.
  • Supportive and collaborative work environment built on accountability and continuous improvement.
  • Thoughtful company culture, including birthday recognitions and team appreciation initiatives.

Working Hours

  • Full-time role, 8 hours per day (excluding a 1-hour break).Â 
  • Schedule details may be discussed during the final stages of the hiring process.Â 
  • Scheduling is flexible; however, team members are required to maintain a minimum of 5â6 hours of overlap with the firm's operating hours in Pacific Time (PT), subject to operational needs and team coordination.

Application Process

Candidates may be asked to complete the following during the recruitment process:

  • Most recent Resume/CV (required).
  • Communication and presentation assessment, including a practical assignment relevant to HR operations, recruitment, or training material creation.
  • Proof of qualifications and professional references. To ensure fairness and accuracy, compensation verification may be conducted for shortlisted candidates.

Additional Information

  • This is a fully remote, South Africa-based role.
  • Engagement is as an independent contractor; tax compliance is the contractor's responsibility.
  • A 3-month probationary period will apply to support onboarding and performance alignment.
  • We are an equal opportunity employer and welcome applicants from all backgrounds.

Due to the high volume of applications we receive, contacting our offices by phone, email, or social media regarding this position is strictly prohibited. Any inquiries about application status through these channels will result in automatic disqualification from the hiring process. Our hiring team carefully reviews every submission and will contact qualified candidates directly.

jobs.description:
The Problem

36 million businesses in America need insuranceâit's not optional. 77% are underinsured. 40% have no coverage at all. The distribution system failed them: too slow, too opaque, too confusing.

Over 90% of commercial insurance is still human-led. We're building the inverse: 90%+ AI-led, pushing toward the higher 90s. Not by patching legacy workflowsâby building AI that makes humans more effective, improves the customer experience, and eliminates friction at every step.

We're adding ~1,000 customers per month. We've grown 100x since last year. We're looking to do even more this yearâand that's why we're hiring.

You'll build the team and the systems the rest of engineering depends on. When they compound, everyone gets faster.

The Thesis

Harper runs 200+ services across Railway and AWS. We orchestrate N parallel agentic workloads. Our AI systems make thousands of decisions a day, and every decision needs to be traceable, evaluated, and cheaper to run tomorrow than it is today. The infrastructure underneath all of that is the difference between a company that scales and one that stalls.

Great platform engineering here isn't invisibleâit's the reason product ships fast. When observability catches a silent failure before a customer does. When a pooling layer makes connection exhaustion a non-issue. When developer velocity doubles because someone built the tool nobody knew they needed. That leverage compounds across every other engineer on the team.

The Role

This role is open both to an experienced EM and to someone on the path to becoming an EM who doesn't yet have significant management experienceâwe're happy to bring that person on and support the transition.

This is a team that still needs to be built. We have 2 people in it today, and we believe this area needs significant investment at Harper. The role owns three things: infrastructure (cloud, third-party vendors, and everything surrounding it), developer productivity (making sure we're genuinely an AI-first shop, with the right AI tooling and harnesses in place for every other engineering team to be successful), and SRE and production support (production discipline is top of mind as we head into a high-growth, high-scale phaseâwe need someone who has run an SRE function before). Each of these three areas can grow into a larger team of its own over time.

The team is 2 people today, growing to five to six over the next three months. Because the team is small, whoever takes this roleâEM or TLMâwill need to be hands-on at the start, working directly with the team and doing the work themselves.

What You'll Do

  • Own infrastructure â cloud, third-party vendors, and everything surrounding it

  • Build developer productivity â the AI tooling and harnesses that make every other engineering team genuinely AI-first

  • Own SRE and production support â bring production discipline as we head into a high-growth, high-scale phase

  • Build out the team â grow from 2 people to five to six over the next three months

  • Stay hands-on â with a team this small, work directly alongside your engineers and do the work yourself, not just direct it

  • Grow each function over time â infrastructure, developer productivity, and SRE/production support can each become a larger team of its own

You Might Be a Fit If...

  • Have at least 2 years as a line manager directly managing teams of six to ten peopleâor clear readiness to grow into that role

  • You've been a line manager for at least two years, directly managing teams of six to ten peopleâor you're on a clear path there and want to grow into it

  • You have hands-on experience with AWS or GCP and strong database troubleshooting skills

  • You've seen real scaleâon the order of at least a million requests per minute

  • You can troubleshoot across databases, networking, compute, Docker, Kubernetes, and other aspects of infrastructure

  • You care as much about developer productivity and AI tooling as you do about raw infrastructure

  • You know on-call practices, SLAs, SLOs, and SRE practices generally

  • You want to stay hands-on and grow into a fuller managerial role over time

  • You move fast, with the same appetite as the rest of Harper

Nice to Have

  • Your own network to draw on for hiringâotherwise, comfort working closely with recruiters

  • Experience building developer productivity tooling and AI harnesses for other engineering teams

  • Experience building a team from a very small base

  • Prior startup experienceâespecially at a company scaling through hypergrowth

Compensation & Logistics

  • Salary: $225,000â$275,000

  • Location: San Francisco, in-office. Based in SF or willing to relocate.

  • Schedule: MondayâFriday, in-office five days a week.

  • Benefits: Uber commuter benefits; breakfast, lunch, and dinner provided; snacks, drinks, and coffee daily; free gym membership; health, dental, and vision insurance.

The Process

  1. Hiring Manager screen - 30 min video chat.

  2. Technical screen â 60 min remote: project deep dive + system design

  3. Super Day on-site â meet the team, sit in on the operation, do real work alongside us.

Hi there, I'm Olive Turon, Head of People & Culture at TestGorilla. I'm excited to share more about the Senior People & Talent Operations Partner role and our team.

About TestGorilla

At TestGorilla, we're on a mission to place 1 billion people in their dream jobs. To democratize opportunity, we're building the world's leading skills-based talent discovery platform - one that replaces reliance on resumes with scientific validation of what people can truly do.

Founded as a 100% remote company in 2020, our global team is united by high standards, a lot of heart, and a relentless drive to conquer new technological frontiers. We're all AI-fluent builders who care deeply about replacing bias with fairness.

After empowering thousands of companies to hire smarter and faster, we're now unlocking the next phase of our scale-up journey - where you'll play an instrumental role in creating a world where skills matter most!

About the role

As our Senior People & Talent Operations Partner, you'll own People Ops as a product: the systems, compliance, and self-serve workflows that let most of People & Culture run itself day to day, plus the tooling behind how we hire. You'll join a lean, two-person team, working directly with me, with proper and lasting ownership from day one.Â 

Payroll, compliance, and HR systems across every (35, currently!) country we operate in are foundational elements of this role. Just as critically, you'll build and own the AI/automation and self-serve layer that keeps our People function lean, bringing a product mindset to everything you touch.Â  Letâs face it: weâre a scale-up, so youâll also need to be happy wearing other People hats when the moment requires.

We're looking for someone autonomous, opinionated and candid, who'll tell me when I've got it wrong. You'll be dealing with real people and real problems, so you'll need to stay empathic but boundaried, structured and organized even when the pace picks up.

Iâm biased, but I think itâs a dream job: this is an HR role in an HRTech company changing the world of work for the better, weâll have immense amounts of fun, thereâs plenty of uncharted territory for you to make your own, and Iâm committed to helping you to do the best work of your life.

A quick check: if you've never built objectively clever automations (not just used one someone else built), this probably isn't the role for you. Automation is just that central to the job.

Responsibilities

In this role, your responsibilities will include:

  • Upholding TestGorilla's behaviors and fostering an inclusive, supportive culture.

  • Designing, building and maintaining a smart, automated and AI-enabled people journey - from pre-boarding to off-boarding - that frees up capacity for bespoke, white-glove treatment where it matters

  • Being the technical owner and orchestrator of our HR tech stack: evaluating and enhancing it, ensuring these tools are not siloed but unified and integrated.

  • Owning the non-Finance side of payroll, invoicing, contract administration, and compliance end to end, across every country we operate in.

  • Owning data privacy and recordkeeping, and the day-to-day relationship with our EOR vendor.

  • Owning configuration and troubleshooting of our hiring tooling, so hiring managers can run their own searches independently.

  • Owning the documentation that makes self-serve actually work in practice, ensuring that itâs structured in a way that is easily accessible to both humans and P&C AI agents.Â 

  • Working with me to maintain a clean line between what's self-serve and what needs a person. We do not aspire to automate our entire People journey here.Â 

What you'll bring

We're looking for someone who:

  • Is passionate about TestGorilla's mission to help one billion people find their dream jobs.

  • Has excellent written and verbal communication skills in English.

  • Has built and owned sophisticated automations (Zapier, n8n, Make.com, and the like) as a core part of an integrated HR tech stack, not just used AI tools day to day. Arguably the most important thing on this list.

  • Has managed payroll, compliance, or HR operations across multiple countries, ideally through an Employer of Record or a mix of EOR and direct entities.

  • Has deep, hands-on HRIS experience. HiBob experience is a big plus, and so is experience assessing or migrating HR systems.

  • Brings a product mindset: builds for the people who use them (employees and managers), listens to their feedback, and iterates rather than building in isolation.

  • Thrives in a high-autonomy, async-first, remote-only environment, and has worked in these kinds of teams and working cultures before.

  • Marries operational rigor with genuine empathy and a real interest in people. You'll be dealing directly with team members, sometimes on sensitive matters.

  • Is opinionated and candid, with excellent feedback and stakeholder management skills.

Most people in this role will have acquired these skills over five years of relevant experience. That being said, we care far more about what you've owned, your impact and how you've progressed, than the exact number of years.

We seek diversity and encourage applications from everyone, even if your experience doesn't exactly match the description. Studies show that women and underrepresented groups can be hesitant to apply unless they meet every requirement - let's buck that trend!

Bonus skills

While these skills aren't a requirement, we'd be very interested to hear from you if you have any of the following:

  • Experience with an ATS or hiring platform such as Ashby, Greenhouse, or Lever.

  • Experience with an EOR provider such as Remote, Deel, or Oyster.

  • HRIS implementation or migration project experience.

  • Experience supporting a team through organizational change.

What's in it for you?

Please note: In this role, you'll be hired as an Individual Contractor.

  • Global Team: Join a fully remote, mission-driven team from around the world.

  • Competitive compensation: â¬56,520 - â¬70,650 base pay + Share Appreciation Rights (SARs). This role doesn't carry a bonus component.

  • Remote & flexible work: Work from almost anywhere*. Enjoy flexible hours and asynchronous work to balance work and life.
    *Check out the countries we currently hire from here.

  • Remote work budget: â¬1,000 available each year, or up to â¬2,000 from day 1 if you're buying a laptop!

  • Growth & development: Invest in yourself and your career with a 3.5% L&D budget per year and clear growth opportunities.

  • Parent/Caregiver support: We provide a caregiver-friendly work environment with paid 8-16 week parental leave and tailored return-to-work approaches.

  • Work-life balance: Our unlimited and flexible time off policy empowers you to take the time you need to recharge and maintain your well-being.

Interested?

At TestGorilla, we believe your skills speak louder than your resume. That's why we champion a skills-first approach, using cutting-edge, AI-powered assessments to uncover your true skills and experience match.

When you apply, you'll get to experience our platform firsthand by taking an assessment â it's your invitation to shine and show us what you can do! While our platform is powered by AI, every hiring decision is made by humans. Check out our Applicant Privacy document to see how we protect your data.

Given the hiring sprint timeline above, we'd love to see your application land before September 20.

Concerned about test anxiety or need help with the assessment? We've got you covered. Please check out our candidate support page for any questions. Accommodations are readily available as part of the assessment setup, and requesting support will never impact your application.

RainFocus, one of the most innovative software companies, is in search of an exceptional Senior Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) Analyst. 

 

About RainFocus

 

RainFocus cares about its employees, customers, and the world in which we live. Our rapidly growing team serves Fortune 500 companies like Adobe, Cisco, IBM, Oracle, VMware, and others to prepare and execute in-person, virtual, and hybrid events across the world. Those events are delivered through our industry-disrupting software platform, with groundbreaking business intelligence, to elevate the attendee experience, streamline event operations, and accelerate marketing results. We are well-funded, growing fast, and building a company that is changing the market â it will be challenging, fun, and exciting.

About the Role

We are seeking a highly skilled and motivated Senior GRC Analyst to join our Security and Privacy team. In this role, you will own and grow RainFocus's governance, risk, and compliance program â maintaining our control framework, leading risk assessments, supporting audits, and driving the program's maturity forward rather than simply maintaining the status quo. You will report directly to the CISO and have significant ownership from day one.

\n


Key Responsibilities:
Lead RainFocus's GRC program across SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, and other client/regulatory compliance frameworks, including audit prep, evidence collection, and auditor relationships.
 
Manage and mature our control framework, mapping new regulations and conducting gap assessments.
 
Own the annual security risk assessment process (NIST SP 800-30 methodology), including stakeholder interviews, risk scoring, and residual risk tracking.
 
Maintain and update security policies, standards, and documentation to ensure compliance with industry best practices.
 
Partner with Engineering and Security to mature vulnerability management and secrets-scanning practices, moving these from reactive to proactive, pre-deployment controls.
 
Help build out and operationalize a Data Loss Prevention (DLP) program, including policy design and rollout across email, endpoint, and cloud storage.
 
Grow and mature RainFocus's security awareness training program.
 
Drive AI governance efforts â policy, tooling, and monitoring for approved vs. unapproved AI tool usage across the company.
 
Identify and help close Shadow IT / unmanaged SaaS visibility gaps in partnership with IT.
 
Collaborate with cross-functional teams to implement risk management practices and ensure compliance across the organization.
 
Respond to security and privacy inquiries from clients, partners, and employees.
 
Prepare and present reports on the organization's security and privacy compliance status, including program maturity and remediation progress.
Stay abreast of emerging security threats, vulnerabilities, and compliance requirements.


Qualifications:

Bachelor's degree in Technology, Cybersecurity, or a related field is highly desirable.

6+ years of proven experience in GRC, IT audit, information security compliance, or a related field.

In-depth knowledge of relevant regulations, standards, and frameworks (e.g., SOC 2, ISO 27001, PCI DSS, NIST 800-series, GDPR, and others).

Experience running or contributing heavily to formal risk assessments â not just tracking a compliance checklist.

Professional certifications such as CISA, CRISC, CISSP, CIPP, or CIPM are highly desirable.

Familiarity with modern security tooling such as Drata, OneTrust, Vanta, etc.

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with keen attention to detail.

Excellent communication and interpersonal skills to work effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders.

Ability to manage multiple projects and meet deadlines in a fast-paced environment.

Experience with cloud security and compliance frameworks is a plus.

Experience with OneTrust or related GRC technologies is a plus.


Personal Characteristics:

Strong work ethic and commitment to excellence.

Ability to work independently and as part of a team.

Excellent problem-solving and analytical skills.

Strong communication and interpersonal skills.

Ability to adapt to change and learn quickly.

Passion for security and privacy.


\n

Job Description

The Surveyor I is an entry or junior-level position for new graduates and/or those candidates with less than five (5) years of experience in an applicable industry. The Surveyor I, under a direct supervisor, performs work involving conventional surveying practices. The primary function is to develop the ability to effectively examine and report on vessels and other marine structures during and after construction relative to compliance with the applicable requirements for maintaining the vessel in Classification with ABS and meeting associated statutory and special service requirements related to Safety of Life at Sea, Loadline, Tonnage, Cargo Gear and Pollution Prevention Certification.

What You Will Do (with the assistance and guidance of an experienced ABS Surveyor):

  • Acts as a professional specialist for the organization in the application of related rules, regulations, requirements, concepts, principles, and processes.
  • Performs routine surveys on classed vessels, platforms, or other marine structures and at manufacturers for classification and compliance with statutory requirements.
  • Prepares technically accurate and timely reports of inspections and surveys performed.
  • Engages in contact with clients to resolve problems within areas of expertise.
  • Maintains survey files in an orderly and up-to-date manner in the area of responsibility.
  • Develops the skills necessary for the administration of office procedures and monitoring of business performance at an assigned port.
  • Through broader and more technically challenging work assignments, the individual must develop a thorough understanding of field operations, policies, methods, and procedures.

What You Will Need:

Education and Experience

  • Qualifications from a tertiary institution within a relevant field of engineering or physical science (minimum two (2) years program); or
  • Qualifications from a marine or nautical institution and relevant seagoing experience as a certificated ship officer, and
  • Proficiency in the English language commensurate with the scope of statutory certification and services and, before assignment, with their future work.
  • Appropriate certification and/or licenses in areas of specialization may be required.

Knowledge, Skills, And Abilities

  • Ability to develop a working knowledge of ABS Rules, Guides, statutory regulations, and related instructions, as well as the ABS Employee Safety Policy.
  • Ability to read engineering plans and have a basic understanding of shipbuilding practices and vessel operations.
  • Ability to perform surveys in the prescribed format.
  • Knowledge of computer programs or software packages related to job responsibilities.
  • Knowledge of related technical interfaces required for group project work.
  • Knowledge of ships' engineering systems and machinery.
  • Ability to communicate, orally and in writing, pertinent information relative to assigned area of technical expertise.
  • Ability to analyze problems and propose solutions.
  • Responsiveness to customers and the ability to work well with others.
  • Ability to become familiar with the ABS Health, Safety, Quality, and Environmental Management Systems.

Physical Requirements:

  • Where allowed by local laws, a pre-employment physical examination is mandatory.
  • The role of surveyor/auditor requires sufficient physical strength, stamina, agility, and both visual and auditory acuity to perform the listed duties effectively.
  • The ability to climb vertical ladders up to nine meters and navigate steep steps is essential.
  • Shall be capable of working at heights on various staging and lifting equipment.
  • Shall be able to maneuver in tight spaces and work inside confined areas for extended periods, including kneeling and crawling.
  • The role may involve exposure to industrial environments, potential injury risks, extreme weather conditions, and demanding physical activities.
  • Shall be able to lift at least 25 lbs. / 11.34 kgs.
  • The use of small tools and the wearing of Personal Protective Equipment (PPE), in accordance with ABS safety procedures, may be required.
  • Where allowed by local laws, the surveyor will be required to successfully complete an annual physical that will recertify the individual can perform the physical actions required.

Reporting Relationships:

Will report to the Principal, Senior, or Surveyor-in-Charge of the assigned port. This position does not have any direct reports.

About Us

We set out more than 160 years ago to promote the security of life and property at sea and preserve the natural environment. Today, we remain true to our mission and continue to support organizations facing a rapidly evolving seascape of challenging regulations and new technologies. jobs.title: Why do you want this new job
jobs.description:
No matter which side of the table youâve sat during interviews, youâve probably heard this question: âWhy do you want this new job?â

In the recent past, Iâve interviewed a few candidates and heard the following answers so far:

  • Iâm not learning much on the current job after itâs been 2-4 years.
  • Iâm looking for something that offers better work-life balance.
  • Iâm not really looking for a job. The recruiters got in touch and I thought Iâd discuss.
  • Iâm looking for more challenging work.

All of the above are valid answers. I think thereâs another perfectly valid answer that candidates seldom mention probably due to the gravity of the interview room situation. Iâve interviewed over a hundred candidates across different companies and am yet to find anyone that mentions: I am not happy with my current salary and benefits compared to my skills

Back to topic of answers. So, when someone answers that they are not learning new things on the job, obviously, youâd be curios to know why and how they have tried to change things. Unfortunately, most candidates simply mention that they are doing repeat work and thereâs not much to learn doing the same thing over and over again. This is where I start feeling a little uneasy. However, I understand that itâs a true statement. If youâre in a similar situation, hereâs some suggestion: read books, and write code based on what youâve read. Then, you can tell a much convincing story that, Iâve forced myself to learn new things and hereâs some proof, but I really want to apply the newly learned skills outside the scope of the âhello worldâ skills.

About work-life balance, I totally hear you. And if your current job doesnât suit what you need out of your life, itâs a perfectly valid reason to look for new opportunities. However, make sure youâre able to clearly set the expectation with your potential employer about what work-life balance means for you. For example, if you canât work over 40 hours a week, or must work from home one-two days a week, itâs best to discuss this even before an interview starts to ensure youâre a good match with the employer.

If you showed up at in interview just because a recruiter got in touch, Iâd say introspect first. Itâs possible that on our subconcious mind you have expectations that the potential of the new job offers you something that you donât get at the current job. So, instead of a passive asnwer that the you simply acted based on the recruiterâs invite, itâs much convincing to see if you can lay down one or two things that you expect from the new job that you donât get at the current job.

About looking for more challenge, it sounds like a cliche unless you can share examples of work that is of challenging to you. May be you like the challenge of using more complicated algorithms, may be you like dealing with a lot of data, may be you like supporting production emergencies, but thereâs gotta be something that you can explicitly mention as challenging. It helps employers to understand if theyâre able to provide you with enough challenge on the job.

Finally, if youâre looking for a new job because the current job isnât paying upto the level of your skills and contributions, make sure to communicate it clearly as well. With salaries and benefits, I find it much easier to work with people that know the actual $ figure thatâll make them happy instead of beating around the bush to create confusions all around. Just be confident and tell what makes you happy. If the employer can afford it, most likely theyâll want to get you onboard as a happy employee. If they canât afford it, theyâll do their best. The key here is to be explicit about what you want and be sure and confident about it.

In a nutshell, when you walk into an interview itâs yours to lose. The potential employer is investing their time and resources and would rather have you hired than having to interview other candidates. As long as you are able to justify why you want the new job, theyâll be quite accommodating.
